newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, as bond yields rise.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, as bond yields rise.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Friday, as funds sold and recent support levels broke, following worse-than-expected U.S. March PPI and retail sales data which drove U.S. bill and bond yields sharply higher.

"With the market and the Fed driving real interest rates higher, precious metals look less attractive, while the weakness in the stock market is not yet pronounced enough to encourage a move into gold," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
In Friday's data, the U.S. March PPI fell 0.1 percent but the core rate, excluding food and energy rose a higher-than-expected 0.4 percent, while U.S. March retail sales rose 0.2 percent.
"But interest in selling gold below $350 is not really there either, with physical demand good below $350 earlier this year, so the downside is probably limited to around $340," Mehta said.
COMEX June gold ended down $1.60 at $349.30, after seeing an intraday low at $348.00, as the contract tested the bottom of the $348.30-358.00 range of the past month.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $346.60/10, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $347.95 and the New York close Thursday around $348.40/90.

Gold has traded in narrow ranges in the past month, with COMEX gold open interest down to its lowest level in a year, but the metal now looks like breaking out to the downside as real interest rates rise in the U.S., lessening the attractions of holding gold, analysts said.

"We believe gold, and to a lesser degree precious metals in general, are fighting an uphill battle against currencies and other financial instruments as wealth safe havens and will maintain a general downward price bias until there is some sign of global inflation," Bear Stearns senior analyst Bill Byers said.

The U.S. dollar has jumped to new five-year highs against the yen and new three-year high against the mark this week. As a result the price of gold in yen terms is back near the highs seen in January 1996, a level at which Japanese disinvestment from gold was seen last year.
COMEX May silver lost 6.20 cents at $4.725 an ounce, after seeing a session low at $4.680, not far from the contract lows seen last week at $4.655.
Spot silver ended quoted $4.73/4.75, not far from the three month low seen last week around $4.70.
But fabrication demand is seen good below $5.00 an ounce limiting the downside, analysts said.
NYMEX July platinum ended down 50 cents at $372.70, but the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread edged higher to $20.00 an ounce.
NYMEX June palladium ended was off 75 cents at $155.00.
But the outloook for platinum group metals remains better than for gold and silver, analysts said, with disruptions to Russian supplies continuing, and auto demand strong.
